source.publication: 2025 Maryland Resident Booklet (State and Local Tax Forms and Instructions), Form 502
source.section: Form 502 Lines 1, 10a, 11, 14-21; Worksheet 13A, NOTE and lines 1-5 (PDF page 14); Instruction 13 Line 10a (PDF page 15); Instruction 10 (PDF page 13); Schedule II (PDF page 22)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private employer pension (you) 50,000.00 + public pension paid by MD (spouse) 30,000.00 + 401(k) distribution (spouse) 5,000.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 = 119,000.00. Taxable Social Security 34,000.00 is the federal Social Security Benefits Worksheet amount on gross benefits 40,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 119,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 2 x 1,600.00 additional for age 65 or older = 84,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 502 Line 1 federal AGI 119,000.00; Lines 2-6 additions 0.00 (no non-Maryland municipal interest); Line 7 total 119,000.00. Worksheet 13A: You (age 70): line 1 qualifying pension 50,000.00; line 2 41,200.00; line 3 Social Security 25,000.00; line 4 tentative 41,200.00 - 25,000.00 = 16,200.00; line 5 smaller = 16,200.00; Spouse (age 68): line 1 qualifying pension 35,000.00; line 2 41,200.00; line 3 Social Security 15,000.00; line 4 tentative 41,200.00 - 15,000.00 = 26,200.00; line 5 smaller = 26,200.00. Line 10a = 42,400.00. Line 11 taxable Social Security in Line 1 = 34,000.00 (exempt in full). Line 14 two-income subtraction: 1,200.00 on the form (both spouses have Maryland income); the projection does not apply it, see the approximation note at the end. Line 15 total subtractions = Line 10a 42,400.00 + Line 11 34,000.00 = 76,400.00. Line 16 Maryland AGI = 119,000.00 - 76,400.00 = 42,600.00. Line 17 standard deduction (Instruction 16, flat by filing status) = 6,700.00. Line 18 net income = 42,600.00 - 6,700.00 = 35,900.00. Line 19 exemptions: Chart 10A at federal AGI 119,000.00 (not over 150,000) gives 3,200.00 each x 2 (Box A) + 1,000.00 x 2 for age 65 or older (Box B, not reduced by the chart) = 8,400.00. Line 20 taxable net income = 35,900.00 - 8,400.00 = 27,500.00. Line 21 tax, Schedule II as numbers: 2.00% x 1,000.00 = 20.00 + 3.00% x 1,000.00 = 30.00 + 4.00% x 1,000.00 = 40.00 + 4.75% x 24,500.00 = 1,163.75; total 1,253.75. (The tax table row 27,500-27,550, PDF page 35, gives 1,255; expected keeps the formula figure.) Lines 22-26 credits: none modelled or claimed, 0.00; Maryland state tax 1,253.75. Local tax (Lines 28-33) out of scope; 2% capital gain tax (Line 21b) not charged (no gains, AGI under 350,000). Line 14 (Worksheet 13D, PDF page 18): the form would subtract the smaller of 1,200 and the lower spouse's income after subtractions = 1,200.00, lowering tax by 1,200 x 4.75% = 57.00; the projection does not apply it (approximation), so expected shows 0.00 here. Each spouse completes a separate column of Worksheet 13A with his or her own Social Security; the two exclusions are combined on Line 10a.
accepted_approximations: The two-income married couple subtraction is not applied.
